LegoAbout.HeroDesc: From a humble carpenter's workshop in Billund to the world's most iconic creativity empire extending to screens everywhere.

1932.title: From Wooden Toys to Legend
1932.desc: Ole Kirk Kristiansen began a journey that would one day lead to the world's largest toy brand by producing wooden yo-yos and toys in a modest workshop in the town of Billund, Denmark.

1934.title: Leg Godt" (Play Well)
1934.desc: The company took its name "LEGO" from the Danish phrase "leg godt," meaning "play well." Little did anyone know it would one day become an empire.

1947.title: First Encounter with Plastic
1947.desc: LEGO purchased Denmark's first plastic injection molding machine. This risky and bold move was the first spark that would transform the company's fate from wood to modern technology.

1949.title: Automatic Binding Bricks
1949.desc: The first prototype of the legendary LEGO brick, "Automatic Binding Bricks," was launched.

1954.title: The Philosophy of the "Play System
1954.desc: Godtfred Kirk Christiansen believed that toys should not be disposable. He realized the idea of a "Systematic Play" where all sets worked together harmoniously, fostering infinite creativity.

1958.title: The Perfect Connection Code: Patent
1958.desc: The patent for the modern LEGO® brick, featuring studs on top and tubes on the bottom, was granted in Denmark at precisely 13:58. The perfect clutch power changed the world.

1968.title: The First LEGOLAND® Opens
1968.desc: The first LEGOLAND theme park that opened in Billund exceeded expectations. While 3,000 visitors were anticipated in its inaugural season, it astonishingly hosted 625,000 guests.

1978.title: The Birth of the Minifigure (History in the Making)
1978.desc: The first LEGO Minifigure, characterized by iconic facial expressions, moving arms, and legs, was launched, marking the reason for our platform's existence. The brick world now had its inhabitants!

1999.title: First Licensed Theme: Star Wars
1999.desc: LEGO ventured beyond its own themes by partnering with Lucasfilm to produce the first Star Wars™ sets. This move became a modern milestone for the company.

2010.title: The Collectible Minifigures (CMF) Craze
2010.desc: The first Collectible Minifigure (CMF) Series 1, consisting of bodies, legs, heads, and accessories sold in closed, surprise bags, hit the shelves.

2024.title: A Continuing Legacy
2024.desc: Today, trillions of bricks have been produced. The minifigure population has already surpassed the human population. And you are part of this magnificent world of collections...

Items.title: Series 1
Items.desc: With yellow heads and 16-figure blind bags, the legend that the whole world would chase was born.

Items.title: Team GB
Items.desc: The first unique step into national and special license concepts was taken with the Great Britain Olympic Team.

Items.title: The Simpsons
Items.desc: For the first time in history, the classic 'yellow cylinder head' rule was broken and IP-based masks/molds were used!

Items.title: Disney S1
Items.desc: Mickey, Ariel, Stitch... It became the most popular CMF series ever, selling out the second it hit the shelves.

Items.title: Series 18 - Classic Police
Items.desc: With only 1 'Classic Police' figure per box, the art of feeling bags turned into a craze.

Items.title: Harry Potter
Items.desc: The first massive 22-figure (two-in-one) series was produced. Innovative bendable midi-legs were invented.

Items.title: The Muppets
Items.desc: A masterpiece with extraordinarily detailed head molds, produced in sculptural quality true to their original forms.

Items.title: Marvel Series 2
Items.desc: With a leap in character designs and item quality, the Marvel Cinematic Universe exceeded toy standards.

Items.title: QR Code Revolution
Items.desc: Bags are gone! Eco-friendly cardboard boxes are here. Scanning the Data Matrix code at the bottom of the box to know the contents shocked everyone!

Items.title: Minifigürlerim
Items.desc: A great page has turned to keep the AFOL culture alive with this Turkey-based premium collection tracking platform!

EvolutionTimeline.Subtitle:
Witness the facial changes of collectible figures from 1978 to present.
Click on the dots to explore the historical evolution.

Items.title: Classic Face
Items.desc: The classic yellow smile was born with Legoland Town.

Items.title: Pirate Era
Items.desc: Beards, mustaches, and eye patches were added.

Items.title: Aliens
Items.desc: Completely different and asymmetrical faces were produced.

Items.title: Freckles & Details
Items.desc: Freckles and lip marks arrived with the Paradisa theme.

Items.title: Spirit of Fire
Items.desc: Effects bursting out from inside the head were designed.

Items.title: Magnifying Glass
Items.desc: Faces at the peak of design technology.

Items.title: CMF Era
Items.desc: Unique collectible faces with the blind bag revolution.

Items.title: Licensed Faces
Items.desc: Custom faces for IP molds like The Simpsons were made.

Items.title: Golden Age
Items.desc: Very rare prints specially made for the 20th anniversary.

Items.title: Modern Era
Items.desc: The level of detail has reached the quality of film studios.

LegoAboutPage.Title: The Bricks of History
LegoAboutPage.Desc: The world's most iconic empire of creativity, from a humble carpenter's workshop in Billund to the screens.

Timeline.title: From Wooden Toys to Legend
Timeline.desc: Ole Kirk Kristiansen started the adventure that would make the world's biggest toy brand by producing wooden yo-yos and toys in a humble workshop in Billund, Denmark.

Timeline.title: "Leg Godt" (Play Well)
Timeline.desc: The company was named "LEGO", a combination of the Danish words "leg godt" meaning "play well". No one knew yet that it would turn into an empire in the future.

Timeline.title: First Encounter with Plastic
Timeline.desc: LEGO purchased Denmark's first plastic injection machine. This risky and bold move became the first spark that carried the company's destiny from wood to modern technology.

Timeline.title: Automatic Binding Bricks
Timeline.desc: "Automatic Binding Bricks", the first prototype of the legendary LEGO brick today, was released.

Timeline.title: "System of Play" Philosophy
Timeline.desc: Godtfred Kirk Christiansen believed that toys should not be disposable. He brought to life the "Systematic Play" idea, where all sets work in harmony with each other and make creativity infinite.

Timeline.title: The Perfect Connection Code: Patent
Timeline.desc: The patent for the modern LEGO® brick with studs on top and tubes on the bottom was obtained in Denmark at exactly 13:58. The perfect Clutch Power changed the world.

Timeline.title: The First LEGOLAND® Opens
Timeline.desc: The first LEGOLAND theme park opened in Billund and shattered expectations. While expecting 3,000 visitors in its first season, it incredibly hosted 625,000 people.

Timeline.title: A Massive Revolution: DUPLO®
Timeline.desc: The DUPLO® series, which has exactly 8 times the volume of the classic LEGO brick, was launched to prevent young children from swallowing it. Interestingly, DUPLO bricks were also fully compatible with classic bricks!

Timeline.title: The Smiling Icon: MINIFIGURE!
Timeline.desc: Designed by Jens Nygaard Knudsen, the legendary "Minifigure" with movable arms, legs, and characteristic yellow face was introduced to the world! Space, knight, and city themes followed one after another that year.

Timeline.title: Pirates and Different Faces
Timeline.desc: For the first time, minifigures went beyond the classic two-dot and a smile mold. With the LEGO® Pirates theme, minifigures with beards, hooks, and eyepatches entered our lives.

Timeline.title: A Galactic Awakening: Star Wars™
Timeline.desc: For the first time in its history, LEGO signed an agreement with a movie license (Star Wars). The first "LEGO Star Wars" set was released, and a commercial legend was born.

Timeline.title: The Legend Rising from its Ashes: BIONICLE®
Timeline.desc: Introduced at a time when the company was in a financial crisis, the story-rich fantasy robot/warrior theme BIONICLE became the hero that almost saved LEGO from bankruptcy.

Timeline.title: Millennium Falcon: The Era of Giants
Timeline.desc: The 5,195-piece First Ultimate Collector Series (UCS) Millennium Falcon was released. The golden age began where LEGO appealed not only to children but also to AFOL (Adult Fans of LEGO).

Timeline.title: Leap to the Silver Screen
Timeline.desc: The legendary "The LEGO Movie" hit theaters and rocked the box office. The movie's song "Everything is Awesome!" turned into a pop music hit.

Timeline.title: A Passion Without Borders
Timeline.desc: Today, LEGO® is the world's most valuable and innovative toy brand. It is a magnificent culture passed down through generations with its philosophy "You are limited only by your imagination", which it frequently emphasizes.
